title: Nf Maxorder Resource
objective: Implement the host-neutral FLINT polynomial-to-HNF order resource boundary and standalone lifecycle/differential tests required by P2

exceptions: A compact FLINT fmpz polynomial-to-HNF resource boundary requires direct ownership and storage primitives not expressible by the current typed compiler; the ordinary Python orchestration and existing Round-2 path remain the correctness fallback.

handoff.summary: Implemented a host-neutral owned number-field order resource. It accepts a sealed monic fmpz polynomial and fmpz prime-hint matrix, builds the equation-order multiplication table inside FLINT, resolves exact unramified hints (including arbitrary-size primes), runs batched word-prime Round 2 without an n^3 host transfer, and publishes canonical HNF numerator/common-denominator bytes with exact index and discriminant evidence. Ramified primes above UWORD_MAX return an explicit capability status and preserve the complete prime for the strict-Python fallback. Standalone C plus independent JS decoding cover lifecycle, sanitizer stress, frozen Sage/PARI-compatible lattices, invalid inputs, and a reproducible benchmark.
risks: The existing Round-2 kernel still uses fmpq internally during basis changes; this boundary canonicalizes to one integer HNF only after the batch. Replacing iterative fmpq arithmetic belongs to the later local-algorithm lane.
A ramified arbitrary-size prime is intentionally capability-fallback, never silently narrowed. Central orchestration must check status before accepting the returned equation-order basis.
Architecture checks require integration-owned native-code classification/audit entries for the new header and C witness. Portable tests also require the integration-owned test runner manifest entry.
next_steps: Add number_field_order_resource_ffi.h to flint headers and declare an owned sagejs_number_field_order_resource_t with clear sagejs_number_field_order_resource_clear, size sagejs_number_field_order_resource_allocated_bytes, and copied_bytes data/length accessors sagejs_number_field_order_resource_data/sagejs_number_field_order_resource_length (wasm=False).

Declare sagejs_number_field_order_from_polynomial_resource as an allocating Status(1) function with out resource plus borrowed FmpzPolynomial and FmpzMatrix inputs; declare the uint64 status/count accessors or decode their fixed transfer metadata. Status 0 is complete, 1 requires arbitrary-prime dynamic fallback, and 2 requires generic native fallback.

Classify the header as mixed-native audit-required (storage boundary plus direct polynomial table and Round-2 dispatch) and the standalone C witness as benchmark-reference accepted; add test/number-field-order-resource-ffi.cjs to the native test tier.
Wire ordinary strict Python orchestration so every nonzero status closes the native result and runs the existing correct dynamic Round-2 branch for the unresolved batch.
